title: Is Namibia Worth Visiting in December? Heat, First Rains and Quiet Waterholes
meta_title: Namibia in December: Desert Heat, Coast and Etosha
meta_description: Namibia in December: weather by region, Etosha and Sossusvlei tips, current fees and a 10-day route. Plan your summer trip with Divulge Adventures.
excerpt: Namibia in December brings dry dunes, a cool coast and busy Etosha waterholes before the rains. Here is the weather by region, current fees and a route that works.
content:
Namibia in December is hot, mostly dry and surprisingly rewarding: the Namib dunes bake under clear skies, the Atlantic coast stays cool at about 22°C, and Etosha's waterholes still draw elephants and lions before the main rains arrive in January. Expect 35°C afternoons inland, a few thunderstorms in the north and busy coastal towns over the holidays.

The hard part of planning Namibia in December is not deciding whether to go, but working out how to arrange the days around the heat, the festive crowds and the patchy rain. Below you will find what each region is really like in December, current fees and entry rules, a route that works, and honest advice on who should pick another month.

Photo by Joe McDaniel on Unsplash

Quick Facts

  • Season: Early summer and the start of the green season; rain arrives first in the north and north-east
  • Etosha: About 35°C highs, 18°C lows, roughly 56 mm of rain on 8 days
  • Sossusvlei: About 29°C highs, 14°C lows, almost no rain, extreme UV
  • Coast: Swakopmund about 22°C by day and 15°C at night, sea around 16°C
  • Park fee: N$280 per foreign adult per day at Etosha and Namib-Naukluft (checked October 2026)
  • Visa: Needed by many nationalities, including UK passport holders; N$1,600 for adults (checked October 2026)
  • Best for: Desert photography, birding, a cool coastal break and travellers who like quieter parks before Christmas

What Is the Weather Like in Namibia in December?

The weather in Namibia in December depends on where you stand. The interior is hot, with highs in the mid-30s around Etosha and late-20s in the Namib, while the coast stays mild and often misty. Rain comes as short afternoon storms, mostly in the north and north-east, and the desert usually stays dry.

Photo by Andrew Svk on Unsplash

Namibia sits in the southern hemisphere, so Namibia in December means early summer. The cold Benguela Current keeps the coastline far cooler than the inland desert, so a day's drive can take you from 35°C to a fleece-and-fog evening in Swakopmund.

The table below uses long-term averages from weather2travel.com (checked October 2026). Treat them as a guide rather than a forecast: some years the first good rains arrive in late November, other years the north stays dry until January.

AreaDay / nightRainWhat it means
Etosha35°C / 18°CAbout 56 mm, 8 daysHot afternoons, storms possible, game still near water early in the month
Sossusvlei29°C / 14°CAlmost noneDry and clear; dunes very hot by late morning
Swakopmund22°C / 15°CAbout 1 mmMild, sometimes foggy, busy with holidaymakers
Zambezi RegionHot and humidAmong the wettest monthsLush and green, but rough tracks and high malaria risk

How much does it rain in Namibia in December?

Rain in Namibia in December is patchy rather than constant. In Etosha you might get a dramatic storm one afternoon and three clear days after it. In the south and the Namib, rain is rare enough that locals talk about it for weeks. The practical effect on most trips to Namibia in December is small: an occasional slippery gravel road, a cooler evening and much clearer air for photographs.

Is Etosha Worth Visiting in December?

Etosha is worth visiting in December if you go early in the month and accept some heat. Waterholes still draw elephants, zebras, springbok and the lions that follow them, and the first rains bring young antelope and fresh green grass. Once heavy rain sets in, game spreads out and sightings take more patience.

Photo by m_oros on Unsplash

The way to watch game in Etosha in December is to sit at a waterhole from first light until about 10am, then retreat to shade. The floodlit waterholes at the rest camps inside the park come into their own on hot nights, when animals drink after dark. Staying inside or right beside the park cuts out long, hot transfers, which matters more in Namibia in December than in any other month; our post on mistakes first-time Namibia travellers make explains why location matters so much here.

Etosha in early versus late December

Early December usually feels like the end of the dry season, with dusty pans and busy waterholes. By late December, if the rains have started, pools form across the plains and animals no longer need the permanent springs. That is when birding takes over: migrant species arrive for the summer and the bush fills with breeding colour.

Insects, heat and malaria near Etosha

Etosha lies in regions that the CDC malaria table for Namibia lists as malaria areas, and December starts the higher-risk wet season. Speak to a travel clinic about tablets, sleep under a net where provided, and cover up at dusk.

Sossusvlei and the Namib Desert in December

Sossusvlei in December is dry, cloudless and very hot by midday, so the whole visit revolves around the cool hours. Averages of about 29°C mask much hotter sand, and the UV index is extreme. Arrive at the gate as it opens, climb a dune at sunrise and be off the pans before the heat peaks.

Photo by JP Desvigne on Unsplash

From September to April the main Sesriem gate opens at 06:00 and closes at 18:00. Guests staying at the two camps inside the gate can use the inner gate from 05:00 to 19:00, which puts them at the dunes for first light before the day visitors arrive. Dune 45 sits 45 km from the gate along a tarred road, and the final 5 km to Sossusvlei and Deadvlei is deep sand: only 4x4 vehicles drive it, and everyone else takes the shuttle from the 2x4 car park (about N$250 return, checked October 2026).

How to plan a Sossusvlei morning in December

A good morning in Namibia in December looks like this: leave camp in the dark, climb Big Daddy or Dune 45 for sunrise, walk to Deadvlei by 8am while the trees still cast long shadows, and be back at the car by 10am. Carry at least two litres of water each. Save Sesriem Canyon for late afternoon. Our 3-Day Namib Desert and Sossusvlei Experience follows exactly this rhythm.

Swakopmund, Walvis Bay and the Coast Over the Holidays

The coast of Namibia in December is cool, dry and lively. Swakopmund averages about 22°C by day and 15°C at night, which feels like air conditioning after the desert. It is also where Namibian families head for the December holidays, so restaurants fill up, activities sell out and the town has a festive, seaside buzz.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

The coast is the easiest place in the country to spend two nights and recover from the heat. The classic December mornings are a dolphin and seal cruise in Walvis Bay lagoon, followed by a 4x4 trip to Sandwich Harbour, where tall dunes drop straight into the Atlantic. Our 4 Days Magical Namibia Safari combines Sossusvlei with exactly this Walvis Bay and Swakopmund stretch.

What to expect from the festive crowds

Swakopmund is the busiest place in Namibia in December, especially between Christmas and New Year. Book accommodation and guided activities well ahead, and expect more traffic on the main road from Windhoek. In early December the town is far calmer, so if you want both the coast and quiet, aim for the first two weeks.

How Much Does Namibia in December Cost?

The fixed costs of Namibia in December are the visa, park fees and activities, and they have risen recently. Foreign adults now pay N$280 per day at Etosha and Namib-Naukluft, and many nationalities pay N$1,600 for a visa. Lodge rates depend heavily on dates, with the Christmas and New Year week usually the most expensive.

Namibia raised its park fees sharply from 1 April 2026, when the Etosha fee for foreign adults went from N$150 to N$280 per day, as reported by Tourism Update in January 2026. The table below lists the fixed costs of Namibia in December that we could confirm in October 2026. Fees change, so always check them again before you travel.

CostAmountNotes

Accommodation is where the cost of Namibia in December varies most. Early December often has good availability and normal rates, while the festive weeks fill fast and some properties charge a supplement. The price of your trip will also depend on whether you choose a guided trip or a self-drive; our guide to guided versus self-drive Namibia trips sets out the trade-offs.

Entry Rules and Health Before You Fly

Entry rules for Namibia changed in 2025, and they matter for Namibia in December because queues at the airport grow over the holidays. Since 1 April 2025 many nationalities, including British travellers, need a visa, which can be bought online in advance or on arrival. Malaria precautions apply in the north, including around Etosha.

The UK government's Namibia entry requirements page confirms that UK citizens can use either the e-visa or the visa-on-arrival route, that the adult fee is N$1,600 and that passports need at least six months' validity and three blank pages (checked October 2026). Applying online before you travel saves time at Hosea Kutako International Airport in a busy month. Other nationalities should check their own government's advice.

Which December Route Works Best?

The best route for Namibia in December runs desert, then coast, then Etosha. You see Sossusvlei while it is dry, cool down by the sea for two nights, and reach Etosha last, when the animals are still close to water. Ten days covers it comfortably; seven days works if you skip the coast.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

The route below suits a first visit to Namibia in December. It keeps the longest drives in the cooler morning hours and puts a pool stop after each desert or game day. For trips that continue to the Okavango, our Botswana vs Namibia comparison explains how the two countries pair up in summer.

DaysWhereWhy in December
1WindhoekArrive, collect visa if needed, rest after the flight
2-3SossusvleiTwo sunrises on the dunes; afternoons by the pool
4-5Swakopmund and Walvis BayCool sea air, lagoon cruise, Sandwich Harbour
6Damaraland or ErongoBreak the long drive north among granite hills
7-9EtoshaWaterhole mornings, floodlit waterholes at night
10WindhoekDrive south and fly home

Who should choose another month?

If your main goal is classic dry-season game viewing in Etosha, July to October is more reliable. Travellers who dislike heat should look at May or June. Hikers should note that the Fish River Canyon trail only runs from 1 May to 15 September, so it is closed in December. Insider Tips

  • Start early: Plan every walk and game drive in Namibia in December for before 10am; the light is better too
  • Book the festive weeks first: Lodges inside Sossusvlei and Etosha, and Swakopmund over New Year, fill first
  • Carry water: At least two litres per person on dune mornings and long drives
  • Drive storms carefully: Gravel can turn slippery after a downpour; slow down and avoid driving at night
  • Pack for two climates: Light cotton for the interior, a fleece for misty coastal evenings
  • Plan malaria cover: Etosha and the north fall in malaria regions; Windhoek and the desert do not

Frequently Asked Questions

Is December a good time to visit Namibia?

Yes, Namibia in December is a good choice if you can handle heat. The desert is dry and bright, the coast is mild at around 22°C, and Etosha's waterholes still draw game early in the month. The trade-offs are 35°C afternoons inland, the first thunderstorms in the north and festive-season demand for rooms.

Does it rain in Namibia in December?

Rain in Namibia in December is patchy and falls mostly in the north and north-east as short afternoon storms. Etosha averages about 56 mm over roughly eight rainy days, while Sossusvlei and Swakopmund usually see almost none. Mornings are generally clear, so game drives and dune walks rarely get washed out.

How hot is Sossusvlei in December?

Sossusvlei in December averages highs of about 29°C and lows of about 14°C, and the open sand feels far hotter by late morning. The UV index is extreme. Enter the park at opening, climb the dunes by 9am and spend the middle of the day resting at your lodge rather than walking to Deadvlei.

Do I need a visa for Namibia in December?

Many visitors to Namibia in December need a visa, including British travellers since 1 April 2025. UK citizens can apply online for an e-visa or buy a visa on arrival at main ports such as Hosea Kutako Airport, and the fee was N$1,600 for adults when checked in October 2026. Confirm the rules for your passport before you fly.

Is Etosha worth visiting in December?

Etosha is worth visiting in December, especially in the first half of the month before heavy rain spreads the animals out. Waterholes still pull in elephants, zebras and predators, the light is softer after storms and the first young antelope appear. Expect hot afternoons, more insects and a need for malaria precautions.

Final Thoughts

Namibia in December rewards travellers who plan around the heat: dry dunes at dawn, a cool break on the coast and Etosha's waterholes before the rains spread the game. Go early in the month for quieter parks, or book well ahead if you want to spend Christmas in the desert.
